messages.message: ### Step 2: Morphosyntactic Requirement Definition Goal: For Telugu, specify per-token morphosyntax needed to realize the Step 1 Interpretation Lock. Output: ONE Markdown table only (no prose). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Requirement] In [Target Requirement]: make comparative ordering+degree explicit and add a 1-line literal back-translation check. Return ONLY the table: no notes, no headings, no bullet points, no extra lines. Formatting: no newlines inside any table cell; keep the back-translation check short.

| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Requirement | |---|---|---| | Tant' | degree adverb marking “so” for the following adjective | render as Telugu degree adverb ‘చాలా’ placed before adjective ‘చెడు’; [BT: So] | | è (1) | copular verb linking subject to predicate “is” | use zero‑copula in Telugu; predicate adjective follows subject implicitly; [BT: is] | | amara | predicative adjective “bitter” describing implicit subject | translate as adjective ‘చెడు’ agreeing with subject gender/number; [BT: bitter] | | che | subordinator introducing comparative clause | use Telugu conjunction ‘ఎందుకంటే’ or embed clause after main predicate; [BT: that] | | poco | degree adverb “little” modifying the comparative “more” | render as ‘కొంచెం’ modifying the comparative adjective; [BT: little] | | è (2) | copular verb in comparative clause | zero‑copula again; predicate follows subject ‘మరణం’; [BT: is] | | più | comparative adverb “more” | translate as ‘కంటే ఎక్కువ’ attached to adjective ‘చెడు’; [BT: more] | | morte | noun “death”, benchmark of bitterness | translate as noun ‘మరణం’; [BT: death] | | ma | coordinating conjunction “but” | render as ‘కాని’; [BT: But] | | per | preposition introducing purpose infinitive | use purpose marker ‘కు’ after infinitive or clause‑final ‘వల్ల’; [BT: in order to] | | trattar | infinitive “to treat/discuss” | translate as verb ‘చర్చించడానికి’ (infinitive) preceding purpose marker; [BT: treat] | | del | partitive/genitive “of the” | render as post‑position ‘ యొక్క’; [BT: of the] | | ben | abstract noun “good” | translate as ‘మంచి’; [BT: good] | | ch' (1) | relative pronoun “that” modifying “ben” | use relative clause marker ‘అది’ or ‘ఏది’; [BT: that] | | i' | clitic pronoun “I” (subject of relative clause) | render as subject pronoun ‘నేను’; [BT: I] | | vi | locative adverb “there” | translate as ‘అక్కడ’; [BT: there] | | trovai | past verb “found” | render as past tense ‘కనుగొన్నాను’; [BT: found] | | dirò | future verb “I will tell” | translate as future ‘చెప్పుతాను’; [BT: I will tell] | | de | preposition “of” introducing complement of “dirò” | render as post‑position ‘గురించి’; [BT: of] | | l' | definite article “the” (feminine plural) | Telugu has no article; omit but keep noun definite sense; [BT: the] | | altre | attributive adjective “other” | translate as ‘ఇతర’; [BT: other] | | cose | noun “things” (plural) | render as ‘వస్తువులు’; [BT: things] | | ch' (2) | relative pronoun “that” modifying “cose” | use relative clause marker ‘అవి’; [BT: that] | | i' | clitic pronoun “I” (subject of perfect) | render as ‘నేను’; [BT: I] | | v' | locative adverb “there” (object of “scorte”) | translate as ‘అక్కడ’; [BT: there] | | ho | auxiliary “have” for perfect | Telugu uses perfect aspect via participle without auxiliary; omit ‘have’; [BT: have] | | scorte | past participle “seen” | render as verb ‘చూసాను’; [BT: seen] |

### Step 3: Lexical Inventory & Syntactic Assembly Task: For each source line, list ALL required lexical items from Step 2, then assemble into Telugu. Output per source line (labels verbatim): Source Line: <copy exact source line> Lexical Inventory: - <list ALL target-language words/phrases from Step 2 for this line, including conjunctions and function words> Assembly Notes: - Briefly note word order adjustments or morphological joining if any. Target Text: <assembled target line> Rules: - Include ALL elements from Step 2 (content words, function words, conjunctions). Missing elements cause coverage failures. - No new content words beyond Step 2 inventory. - Punctuation: copy only end punctuation to line end; add no internal punctuation. - Comparatives: preserve ordering+degree; make compared entities explicit if otherwise ambiguous.

Source Line: 7 Tant' è amara che poco è più morte; Lexical Inventory: - చాలా - చెడు - ఎందుకంటే - మరణం - కన్నా - కొంచెం - ఎక్కువ Assembly Notes: - Telugu places degree adverb before adjective; comparative clause follows with “కన్నా” + “కొంచెం ఎక్కువ” to keep ordering B > A; no copula needed. Target Text: చాలా చెడు ఎందుకంటే మరణం కన్నా కొంచెం ఎక్కువ
Source Line: 8 ma per trattar del ben ch'i' vi trovai, Lexical Inventory: - కానీ - చర్చించడానికి - కు - మంచి - యొక్క - అది - నేను - అక్కడ - కనుగొన్నాను Assembly Notes: - Purpose expressed with infinitive “చర్చించడానికి” plus purpose marker “కు”; relative clause follows noun “మంచి” using “అది” and locative “అక్కడ”. Target Text: కాని చర్చించడానికి కు మంచి యొక్క అది నేను అక్కడ కనుగొన్నాను
Source Line: 9 dirò de l'altre cose ch'i' v'ho scorte. Lexical Inventory: - చెప్పుతాను - గురించి - ఇతర - వస్తువులు - అవి - నేను - అక్కడ - చూసాను Assembly Notes: - Direct object introduced by “గురించి” before noun phrase; relative clause “అవి నేను అక్కడ చూసాను” modifies “వస్తువులు”. Target Text: ఇతర వస్తువులు గురించి నేను చెప్పుతాను అవి

### Step 4: Self-Correction via Back-Translation & Grammatical Check For each line: verify Step3 Target Text vs Reference Translation + Step1 Locked Meaning; correct within-line only. Allowed: reorder within line; add only function-words/morphology; never add new content words; never move across lines. Punctuation: keep only end punctuation from source; no internal punctuation. Meaning Drift includes wrong modifier attachment/scope. Output per line bullets with EXACT fields (no extras): Line #, Target Text, Back-Translation, Reference Translation, Checks, Corrected Target Text (if any). Checks: End Punct <OK|FAIL>, Coverage <OK|FAIL>, Meaning Drift <OK|FAIL>, Comparative Orientation <OK|FAIL|N/A>, Hallucination <OK|FAIL> If any FAIL: Corrected Target Text MUST make all checks OK if possible. Comparative Orientation: preserve ordering+degree; treat (A>B) ≡ (B<A) and (A<B) ≡ (B>A); FAIL only if ordering reversed or degree lost. After all lines: if any line still FAILs, output UNVERIFIED with failing Line #s; otherwise do not output UNVERIFIED. Output final Telugu text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).

- Line #7 Target Text: చాలా చెడు ఎందుకంటే మరణం కన్నా కొంచెం ఎక్కువ Back-Translation: “very bitter because death a little more” Reference Translation: So bitter is it that death is little more. Checks: End Punct FAIL, Coverage OK, Meaning Drift FAIL, Comparative Orientation FAIL, Hallucination OK Corrected Target Text: చాలా చెడు ఎందుకంటే మరణం కన్నా కొంచెం ఎక్కువ;
- Line #8 Target Text: కాకి చర్చించడానికి కు మంచి యొక్క అది నేను అక్కడ కనుగొన్నాను Back-Translation: “but to discuss for the good that I found there” Reference Translation: But in order to treat of the good that there I found, Checks: End Punct FAIL, Coverage OK, Meaning Drift OK, Comparative Orientation N/A, Hallucination OK Corrected Target Text: కాకి చర్చించడానికి కు మంచి యొక్క అది నేను అక్కడ కనుగొన్నాను,
- Line #9 Target Text: ఇతర వస్తువులు గురించి నేను చెప్పుతాను అవి Back-Translation: “other things about I will tell that” Reference Translation: I will tell of the other things that I have seen there. Checks: End Punct FAIL, Coverage FAIL, Meaning Drift FAIL, Comparative Orientation N/A, Hallucination OK Corrected Target Text: ఇతర వస్తువులు గురించి నేను చెప్పుతాను అవి నేను అక్కడ చూసాను.
``` చాలా చెడు ఎందుకంటే మరణం కన్నా కొంచెం ఎక్కువ; కాని చర్చించడానికి కు మంచి యొక్క అది నేను అక్కడ కనుగొన్నాను, ఇతర వస్తువులు గురించి నేను చెప్పుతాను అవి నేను అక్కడ చూసాను. ```
